clue.text: American's crazy proposal to get things moving

blocks.note: loco is American slang for mad
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A wild American scheme dreamed up to get a stalled project going again.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the power of travelling from place to place, the means by which vehicles and creatures are set going.

clue.text: Put cover over article

indicators.note: a cover placed over something encloses it from all sides

blocks.note: a lid covers a pot
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to drape a cloth over some item.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tense verbs for placing something down, as in 'laid the book on the table'.

clue.text: Gun-runner?

blocks.note: first meaning: a revolver of the famous American make
second meaning: a young male horse, a racer

explanation.walkthrough: A gun-runner smuggles weapons; split in two, the halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Colt's firm made the classic six-shooter, and a young stallion is called by the same word.

clue.text: Learn how to swim -brilliant performance

blocks.note: to master a skill is to learn it fully
a stroke is a style of swimming

explanation.surface: Mastering swimming praised as an outstanding achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterstroke is an outstandingly clever or skilful move, a brilliant piece of work.

clue.text: Bound to be without sovereign -— it's spent

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: bound with rope is tied
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Destined to be short of a pound coin, since the money has all gone.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old gold pound coin, which drives the surface about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means exhausted, worn out, used up, just as a weary person is.

clue.text: Sheds unfashionable businesses

blocks.note: out of fashion
a house is a firm, as in a publishing house

explanation.surface: Sounds like dropping companies that have gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' looks like a verb meaning discards; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Outhouses are small outbuildings next to a main house, such as garden huts or stores.

clue.text: Definite concern

blocks.note: first meaning: settled, fixed, not open to change
second meaning: a business or company

explanation.walkthrough: 'Definite concern' reads like a real worry; concern here is the noun for a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm offer is a fixed one, and a firm is a commercial company, which is also called a concern.

clue.text: Is it a line I rewrote that's okay with leading characters?

indicators.note: something rewritten has been recast in a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer queries whether a revised line of theirs will pass with capital letters at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading characters are the first letters of one's names, so approval given that way is signing with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To initial a document is to approve it by writing your first letters; the -ise form was a verb for this.

clue.text: Christian, for example, not involved in second robbery

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside the robbery phrase

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
taken as written
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: Insisting a churchgoer had no part in a second raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians believe in a single God, so are an example of someone holding that belief.

clue.text: Picture put right inside ailing American gallery

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within the gallery's name

blocks.note: ailing means unwell
standard abbreviation
the Tate is the famous London art gallery
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An instruction for hanging a painting correctly in a gallery belonging to a sick American.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery; 'Picture' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to depict or show it in an image, which is what illustrating does.

clue.text: Deportment one's required in soldiers

indicators.note: something required in a group must be placed among its members

blocks.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'one is'
soldiers as ordinary troops are men

explanation.surface: Good bearing is a quality the army demands of its troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or manner, the way they carry and conduct themselves.

clue.text: Spanner falling down from the air

definitions.text: Spanner falling down from the air

blocks.clueFragment: Spanner falling down from the air
blocks.note: surface reading: a wrench dropped from a height
setter's reading: a thing that spans a river, falling down in a song or tune

explanation.walkthrough: A spanner is a wrench, but also anything that spans; the air is the nursery-rhyme tune whose first line says this structure is falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames crossing in the City is the subject of the children's rhyme about it falling down.

clue.text: Expert who ought to know a good deal?

definitions.text: Expert who ought to know a good deal?

blocks.clueFragment: Expert who ought to know a good deal?
blocks.note: surface reading: a specialist expected to be very knowledgeable, or a shrewd bargainer
setter's reading: deal is pine or fir timber, so this expert knows about trees

explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a word for softwood planks of pine or fir; the specialist in trees should recognise good timber.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies trees and woody plants, so would be expected to judge quality wood.

clue.text: Recalled representative entering plant

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a reed is a tall waterside plant
a Member of Parliament represents constituents

explanation.surface: A delegate was sent back after going into a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory but is the vegetable kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tense verbs meaning brought back to mind.

clue.text: Instrument for cross-country vehicle

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a tractor drives across fields

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a tool kit for an off-road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is a geometry tool used for measuring angles, a drawing instrument.

clue.text: It's specially true, medical checks needed for old people

indicators.note: specially suggests something made to order, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
scans are medical imaging examinations

explanation.surface: A claim that health screening is particularly needed by the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' sounds like pensioners, but means an ancient nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were an ancient civilisation of central Italy, absorbed by Rome, so a people of long ago.

clue.text: Expert on body making a military alliance obscure

blocks.note: taken as written
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
to mist is to blur or obscure

explanation.surface: A scholar of some sort who is making a defence pact hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist studies the structure of living bodies, so is a specialist on them.

clue.text: Search for sign to remove -- see inside

indicators.note: inside places the short piece within the proofreader's mark

blocks.note: dele is the proofreader's mark meaning delete
v. abbreviates Latin vide, see

explanation.surface: Hunting for a notice to take down, and being told to look within.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig deep or research thoroughly, which is to search hard.

clue.text: Go in/out of forbidden territory

indicators.note: out of means taken from within the following words, a run of letters lifted from them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A notice at the edge of a no-go zone about coming and going.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash makes 'in/out' look like a pair of opposites; 'Go in' alone is the definition and 'out of' points to letters sitting in forbidden territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in somewhere is to come or pass into it, the plain sense of this verb.

clue.text: Their burning passion leads to offensive behaviour

definitions.text: Their burning passion leads to offensive behaviour

blocks.clueFragment: Their burning passion leads to offensive behaviour
blocks.note: surface reading: zealots whose fervour makes them obnoxious
setter's reading: people literally keen on setting things on fire, which is a crime

explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning passion' is usually figurative; here the passion is for burning, and 'offensive' means criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: These criminals deliberately set fire to property, so their enthusiasm is literally for burning.

clue.text: See jet land in industrial region

blocks.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a land is a country

explanation.surface: Watch an aircraft touch down in a manufacturing area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet land' suggests a plane landing; jet is the colour. The Black Country is the heavily industrialised area west of Birmingham in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The English district got its name from the soot of its coal mines, foundries and factories.

clue.text: A synthetic that's not new —- only name is changed

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A man-made fibre that has been around a while has just been rebranded.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon was among the first artificial fibres, dating from the 1930s, so is a long-established synthetic material.

clue.text: Additional fruit maiden's abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: plums are fruit
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Some extra fruit that a young woman has left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus as an adjective means extra or added, as in 'a plus factor'.

clue.text: Dramatist's lady taking no notice, repeatedly

indicators.note: taking no means having none of it, so those letters are removed
repeatedly means the remaining letters are written down twice in a row

blocks.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A playwright's leading lady ignores everything again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: LADY without AD leaves LY; 'repeatedly' doubles it. John Lyly was an Elizabethan playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lyly was an English dramatist of the 1580s, author of Euphues and court comedies.

clue.text: Legal documents read out in top-class hotel

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

blocks.note: writs are written court orders

explanation.surface: Court papers being recited in a luxury hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ritz is the famous luxury hotel in London's Piccadilly.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is so tied to luxury that 'ritzy' means plush and expensive, the epitome of grand hotels.

clue.text: Hang about as Dolly repeatedly has ring replaced

indicators.note: replaced means the round letter is swapped out each time for a different vowel

blocks.note: the name written twice
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Waiting around while Dolly keeps swapping her wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: The O is replaced by I in the first Dolly and by A in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilly-dally is to dawdle or waste time, which is to hang about.

clue.text: Fish from either end of dinghy

indicators.note: an end of a word is its first or its final letter

blocks.note: one end of the word
either ... or offers a choice, so the alternative is written as the little word between the ends
the other end of the word

explanation.surface: Catching a fish off the bow or stern of a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Either end of dinghy is literally 'D or Y'. A dory is also a small boat, which suits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is an edible sea fish, often simply called a dory.

clue.text: Spectators see chap finishing second in horserace

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the name of the famous race
finishing means ending up, here placed ahead of the race's name in the final word

blocks.note: a man's name, used for any chap
the Derby is the classic flat race run at Epsom
standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Racegoers watch a man come second in the big race.
explanation.walkthrough: The chap comes first, 'finishing' with the race after him, and S sits inside DERBY. The Derby is England's most famous flat race.
explanation.definitionFit: Standers-by are onlookers or bystanders, people who watch events without taking part.
